title: Atlanta Falcons Head Coach Kevin Stefanski OTA Media Availability | June 8, 2026 | Press Conference
text: Heat. Heat. Heat. Good to see you guys. All right. Uh third week of OTAAS here. So we got three OTAAS this week. Uh today, tomorrow, Thursday, then we're into mini camp next week. Uh you know, he's a younger player, um but has has seen a lot, has been through a lot, if you will, has had different experiences that I think he's certainly willing to share with his teammates. Hey Kevin, in these few months of ramping up, can you elaborate on the resource that that Matt Bryant has been for you as you've gotten to know him? >> Sure. >> Uh yeah, I think Matt has done a a terrific job uh just in terms of helping a bunch of different departments, if you will. Uh but he's just a a been a tremendous uh resource certainly for me uh certainly for our coaches, but I think you see him touching all aspects of this building. >> How how has he impacted you personally? Uh certainly, as you get the pads on, we've talked about don't don't te uh don't grade too much of these offensive and defensive linemen without pads on. Let's let's not let's be careful there. You evaluate everything when you're making decisions on on your players. Uh but certainly, you understand that uh as you get into training camp and you get into preseason games and those type of things, you do weigh it differently. So, we've had guys on the offense, defense, and special teams there. Uh, I just think that program, uh, is has been so impactful in this profession. There's so many great coaches that have come at right out of that program. So, uh, it's and it's a competitive program to to be selected. So, uh, really happy for those guys. I think they're they're getting as much out of it as we're getting uh from them. Kevin, last week we were talking to Jeff about Jaylen Walker. Um and I just kind of want to get your perspective on what you see out of him as a player. U specifically at that at the >> Sure. Uh, and as we all know, that versatility piece, uh, having a defender that can both rush the passer, can stop the run, and can drop into coverage, I think, is is very important for a defense and for a defense coordinator like Coach Brick. Uh, but all those things on the field that that he does are I I think u the versatility would probably be the the main piece. Uh, and then obviously you talk about off the field, the impact that he has on our football team as well. >> Coach, in Cleveland, you brought your basketball and back to OTAAS at mini camp to try to break up some of the monotony and >> do some team chemistry stuff. >> Are you doing anything like that in your first year here? >> We do have a basketball hoop out there. Uh as you become a team, uh there are certain things that we will do. Yes. from a team building standpoint, things that we've done that are great, but it's just as valuable to go sit in this cafeteria and break some bread with a teammate or get out of this place and go to a Braves game or or go wherever, go bowling. title: Exclusive Interview with OC Brian Angelichio | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: What has it been like for you being part of almost [music] an entirely new staff, getting that prep work going before the players got here, and then having [music] them here? >> Yeah, it's been a It's been a fun, exciting process. Certainly, you know, I knew some of the guys having worked with Coach McCarthy previously and James Campen. But, it's been good, you know, getting through, kicking through ideas, seeing what direction we want to go with the offense, you know, blending the terms, you know, stuff that Mike has done in Dallas and certainly stuff in Green Bay, using everybody's experiences, and what's the best way to um you know, put together the plan, the system. >> Is it surreal? How would you describe just being back with Mike McCarthy and some of the others that you mentioned? [music] >> Yeah, it's been great. It's good to see old faces. You know, stayed in touch with a lot of these guys even though it's been, I think, 9 years [music] since we all worked together. So, we're probably not as good a shape as we were, and we're a little grayer, but it's been It's been really fun. >> What is [music] a working relationship like with an offensive coordinator and a head coach who calls the plays? In terms of logistics, whether it's throughout the week, on game days, and then how do you game plan? >> Sure, yeah. You know, obviously, with Mike being the play-caller, and he's very involved in the offense, you know, he's in the offensive meetings, he's in the game plan meetings. So, you're just an extension of Mike. You know, he can't be everywhere, so you know, the meetings with the players, you know, we'll split those up, and you know, I'll try to obviously take a lot [music] of the load off of him and be able to run the staff meetings with the with the staff when we're going through practice, reviewing tape. And then when Mike's in there, obviously, he he'll he'll be in there, but he he uh he does a great job of letting the offensive staff go and and do our thing, and uh certainly, you know he's the checks and balances, right? So he he's got to stroke it if it's if it's good and if he [music] wants to change something certainly we're going to do that. >> How would you describe the offense that you guys are building and preparing for? >> It's it's exciting. I think it's a blend. I think anytime you you build an offense you know with the experience with our staff you know we have some guys that have been doing it quite a while. I think you always try to fit what your players do well and we've kind of done you know so many different things throughout our coaching careers so we're going to take you know certainly core principles of the West Coast offense that have been very successful through a lot of years during coach McCarthy's time. Then it will all start with >> [music] >> the quarterback. Everything that um that will do will go through the quarterback and and the game is seen through the quarterback um to make him successful. So um that part's been fun. That's been exciting and then you take those areas and then you try to do what your players do well and uh try to maximize their abilities and give them the the the resources and the plays that will help them. >> So does it work for any quarterback or is it you're going to go to their strengths? >> Well I think that the training of the quarterback is going to be trained in the West Coast. Everything's going to start with the footwork and to your point if the quarterback's not comfortable with a play we're not going to run that play. I think that's cuz he has the hardest job of anybody on the offense. You know he's got to go to the line, get his pre-snap reads, adjust protections and he's got to you know take his drop, his footwork and deliver the ball so it's got to be things that the quarterback is comfortable with and as things happen quarterback's not comfortable with something it's usually not going to make the game plan cuz he's not confident in the play. >> I saw one of the Green Bay Beat reporters was saying at practices you were always a booming voice, a loud voice, and you're very show and tell. Is that how you would describe your coaching philosophy and teaching? >> Uh I think I've probably mellowed some as I've gotten older, but I think I'm I try to be someone that's honest, you know where I'm coming from. So, I think there shouldn't be any gray area. Um but I just try to be authentic, passionate about the game, and and really try to give the players everything that I could give them, and and along that way you hope to earn the trust. >> You have a lot of experience coaching tight ends. How would you describe what their role is currently in today's NFL? >> Yeah, I think it's it's it's certainly a position that has morphed into a lot of different ways. But they're a valuable piece, particularly when you can get tight ends that are able to you know be a weapon in the pass game. That seems to be the the starting point now in this league where those guys are important on third downs, red areas, you know, first, second down in the play pass game. And then, you know, they got to be able to block. So, the the defense has to respect the run game when they're on the field. So, they're valuable players if you can get those tight ends that can can can really be successful in both.

title: Bears and Indiana stadium news a 'leverage play' - Mike Florio | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: The stadium game continues in Illinois and Indiana. The Bears announced on Friday that on Thursday the team's board of directors voted to advance the potential construction of a new stadium in Hammond, Indiana. Which ultimately means nothing. Until the paperwork is signed, until the shovels are in the ground, until real money is being spent on building a stadium in Hammond, Indiana, it is a leverage play for Illinois. And it's been comical to see some of the people in the media trying to twist themselves in knots by saying, "It's real. It's not leverage. It's real." No, it's leverage because the door is still open in Illinois. It's necessarily leverage. Obviously, until you have focused on one and you've proceeded and there's no way you can go anywhere else, it is leverage for what they also could do in Illinois because they're not trying to apply leverage to Hammond. They got what they want in Hammond. They're not trying to get a better deal out of Indiana. They're trying to get a better deal or any deal out of Illinois. Hammond is the leverage for Illinois. The question is whether Hammond is a bluff. That's the question. And it could be that Hammond started as a bluff, but if it doesn't get us anywhere close to what we want to do and the only alternative is to stay at Soldier Field, then the bluff becomes the play. That's my question. It's obviously leverage and it's disingenuous if not false to call it otherwise. It may be a real option, but it's also leverage because they're still talking to Illinois. And they're apparently still talking to Chicago, even though they say the only options are Hammond, Indiana, and Arlington Heights, Illinois. >> Well, if I recall correctly, didn't the board of directors also vote to advance the Arlington Heights project at one point? title: Reports suggesting A.J. Brown leaked information are disappointing | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: Monday edition of PFT Live, so I was semi-unplugged last Thursday and Friday for my niece's wedding and John Marks, a radio host in Philly at 97.5, I believe, reached out to me and and said, "Hey, have you seen this thing where all of these accounts on Twitter and all these media outlets are claiming that A.J. Brown told Maria Taylor in their interview from last week that he deliberately leaked stories to the media during his time with the Eagles in an effort to motivate his teammates." They're claiming that he said he leaked stories and he never said he leaked stories. So, when I got home and I got settled in yesterday, I went back and watched the interview. And I Look, don't take my word for it, as if you ever will. Here is the question with the answer that has generated a widespread presumption and claim that A.J. Brown told Maria Taylor that when he was in Philadelphia, he leaked stories to the media in an effort to motivate his teammates. Here it is. >> Did you feel as though the picture was making you out to be a villain in some sorts of ways? >> I wouldn't say a villain because some of the things that that was done, it was it was done purposely to give us a push. >> Mhm. >> You know? I know if I say something in the media, I know it's going to propel propel us to work on it cuz now everybody's talking about it. You know? So, it's like, are we going to really going to fix it or not? You know? We can't keep saying that. We can't keep saying it's the standard. It's the standard. And we're not trying to truly get better. Not saying that we were, but but I know if you say what you need to say in the media, which I won't do that anymore, but it gives everything legs and legs to push and and to to push everybody to be to be better. >> So, you felt like basically some of the things you were saying in the media in ways were a strategy in hopes of helping your team get to become the best version of themselves. >> No nothing I ever said was for personal gain. It was always to help this team win and try to be our better self. >> If you're waiting to hear the word leaked, it it's not going to happen because that that's it. There was a follow-up that kind of amplified the point. There's a fundamental difference between saying things in the media and leaking. He's talking about his comments on the record. And this idea that he leaked, like that created this sense of almost sabotage. Saboteur! You're leaking. You're going rogue. You're you're running you know, to to hold hold hold put this out there. Put this out there to motivate the team and it it's just false. And that's what is so depressing. And I know in this day and age, when you start scrolling this phone, there's a good chance half of it is complete and total crap and good luck figuring out what is what. But it's depressing when people who are in the media, who are supposedly like real media outlets or real media figures, eat the trash on something like this and don't go back and watch it. And I think I don't know, but I think it all started with the Dove Climate account on Twitter, which isn't Dove anymore. That guy sold more than 2 years ago. I have the DMs when he told me he was selling the account. I don't know how you sell a Twitter account, but he said he was going to and he apparently did. And I don't know who runs that thing now. But, you know, it's all about engagement farming. It's about And I don't know how I don't try to make money off of Twitter. It's there to just like make our content available to people who are in that space. But, I guess there's a financial incentive to getting more likes and reposts. I don't know. But, that's what apparently caused all this. And you got people like Trey Wingo, sorry to call him out, but he he ate the trash on this. He didn't go back and listen to the interview and apply his own common sense based upon his years of experience. And it just became this presumption that A.J. Brown is out there doing this awful thing of And it is awful if you're doing it. If If he had said, "I Hey, you know what? I went behind everyone's back and I was pulling the strings on the media and I was telling them stuff. I was telling them secrets that shouldn't have left the locker room or the meeting room or the practice field. I was telling these secrets in an effort to make the team better." Yeah, that's a big deal. But, it didn't happen. And I'm still waiting for people. I haven't checked lately. I'm still waiting to see if people will go back and fix it because he did not say that he leaked anything to the media. >> Well, it's not only that, but it's like if you were paying attention to the Eagles for the past few seasons, you know what A.J. Brown was saying to the media. And we have sat in these chairs on this show and talked about how A.J. Brown is trying to motivate his team by going through the media to send a message. So, this is not The The fact that it's like, "Oh, these leaks. This This is What the hell would A.J. Brown need to leak?" Because A.J. Brown's been saying it to everybody's face. So, like that's where I'm like, "Hey guys, like what are What are we doing? What are we talking about? Like could you even think of an instance where there would have been some sort of {quote} leak that would have been damaging to the Eagles or whatever?" And it's obviously he's trying to say Like, "No." A.J. Brown has been very direct about what his thoughts have been about the Eagles as a team and particularly the Eagles as an offense. Right? So, that like I just The whole thing of this like getting in our media ecosystem was so weird to me because I mean, I understand the engagement farming aspect of all of this. but like if we just sit and think about this for 2 seconds, A.J. Brown is not the kind of guy that has ever needed to leak something because he just says it on the record. It's something that I respect about him as somebody who gets paid to talk about football as a living. >> And I think this is a good example of why in this day and age it's important for the consumers to understand that you need to get your information from media outlets that get the bigger picture and aren't just repeating and regurgitating and chasing those clicks. And recognizing, "Ooh, this is a good story. This will This This will register a lot of views. Let's just get it posted without taking a step back and asking ourselves if we should or if it's even accurate." And to your point, A.J. Brown has been very open about his concerns with the team. His comments from last November, which came the day after he was on the Twitch stream and he said, "If you're If you've got me on your fantasy team, get rid of me." He talked about it at the locker. He He said what his concerns were about the offense, and I remember sitting here and saying, "He's so selfless as it relates to making the team better that he's willing to come off as selfish. He's willing to invite the criticism that you're just a diva who wants the football." When what he's trying to do is get the team prepared for single elimination football. Because it doesn't matter if we're winning. If the offense isn't evolving and growing and changing, you're going to get into a spot where you're going to lose because of your offense. And what happened? They weren't able to score when they were in a position to get enough points to beat the 49ers and advance to the division round of the playoffs. So, he ultimately was right. And hey, if he's going to leak anything, he would have leaked his version of why he and Jalen Hurts don't like each other anymore. If A.J. Brown was going to leak one thing, it would have been a Sunday Splash report from Schefter or Rappaport or Glazer with A.J. Brown's version of why he and Jalen Hurts don't get along. Why Jalen Hurts won't throw the ball to him when he's wide open. We would have had that. If he was inclined to leak, that's what he would have leaked. The whole thing The whole thing is very disappointing. And uh but it but it it's also encouraging because folks folks, you got to be careful about where you get your information. And we're always going to tell you the truth informed by our own experience, common sense, and a broader understanding of what people have said and how this thing works. Uh at least we're going to try to. And most of the time we succeed, I think. >> All right, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. title: Brandon Aiyuk calls out San Francisco 49ers in social media post | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC

Say, "I'm here, I'm ready to work, I'm ready to practice, put me on the field." And when they recognize the potential for a $26 million injury, that's when they're going to cut him.
